messages.content: I am trying to keep a few balcony plants healthy through hot weather and a short absence. What would you think through first?
If you're worried about your plants during the heat and while you're away, my first suggestion would be to check how much water your plants actually need. Different plants have different needs!

I'm glad you both said the same thing. It makes me feel like I'm on the right track. I've got a few herbs and some small flowers, but I'm not sure how much they need. Do you think I should water them more now, or is there a better way to prepare?

Since you have different types of plants, it's really helpful to know exactly what they are to give specific advice! Generally, in very hot weather, it's best to check the soil's moisture level directly rather than just sticking to a schedule.
That's good to know. I'll go check the soil then. I was also wondering, do you think I should move any of them out of the direct sun? Some of the leaves are starting to look a little droopy.

request.system: You are a helpful AI assistant in an ordinary conversation. Respond naturally to the participant's message.

result.content: Moving them out of the direct sun sounds like a very good idea right now, especially if they are starting to look droopy. If you're worried about the heat, putting them in a spot that gets filtered or dappled light should help significantly.
